(P. SHIVARAJ)
 Vth Addl. S.C.Judge & 24th ACMM  SCCH-20, Mayohall Unit, Bangalore  JUDGMENT Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.5,00,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 12.12.2018 at about 08.50 AM, on Marathahalli main road, near purvankar rivera, when petitioner was crossing the road cautiously, wherein the driver of the vehicle bearing reg No.KA-53-EY-8270 drove it with high speed rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to the Yashomathi Hospital and later he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient till 12.01.2019 further he was admitted to Manipal hospital,
wherein he took treatment as inpatient till 12.01.2019.
Petitioner has sustained severe traumatic brain injury, multiple carnival fracture, deep vain thrombosis and he has more than Rs.1,00,00,000/- for his medical expenditure.
Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was aged about 38 years and he was working as Chartered accountant in Wipro company and was earning Rs.2,50,000/- per month.
Further petitioner stated that the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, has insured his vehicle with respondent No.2.

He further stated that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.114/2018 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioner stated that respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2 and they are responsible to pay the compensation amount.
He prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent No.1 being owner of the two wheeler has not chosen to file the written statement.
Respondent No.2 filed the written statement by denying the entire petition averments in toto.

4. Respondent no.2 contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and respondent No.1 has intentionally allowed the drive of two wheeler to drive the same without having valid driving license and he has violated the policy conditions and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text:
7. On the basis of pleadings my learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 12.12.2018 at about 08.50 AM, on Marathahalli road near purvankar rivera, Bangalore which was due to rash and negligent driving of motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-EY-8270 by its rider?
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the affirmative,
Issue no.2: In Partly Affirmative
Issue No.3:

As per final order  for the following:
Vaibhav Saha vs Koushik C on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186624589/
3  REASONS  9. Issue No.1 & 2 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
In order to prove the actionable negligence, petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, final report, discharge summaries which are at Ex.P.1, 2, 10 to 14.

10 . On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Sandeep Kumar S/o Rajashekara was the driver of the offending vehicle and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
In the cross examination of PW-1 he clearly denied the suggestion that accident occurred due to his negligence.
Respondent No.2 fails to elicit material facts from the mouth PW-1 to establish his contention nor he has prove his contention as contended in the written statement.
Hence, the version of the respondent No.2 cannot be accepted.

11. The final report which is at Ex.P10 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and deserved to be accepted.

12. Petitioner has tender the discharge summaries which are Ex.P.11 to 14, the entries therein reveals that he has undergone surgeries on 12.12.2018 and on 24.12.2018 for the brain injuries and multiple fractures as stated therein.
It is true from the aforesaid documents that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in Columbia Asia and Manipal hospitals nearly for a period of 10 months.

The respondent No.2 has not disputed nor disprove the details of treatment and medical expenses incurred by the petitioner and he simply denied the quantum of medical expenditure as put forth by the petitioner.
According to petitioner, insurance company has paid the entire medical expenses by securing the original medical bills.
Ex.P.17 is the bank account statement of the petitioner.
As per the entry therein dated 13.12.2019 petitioner has repaid Rs.11,57,880/- to the respondent No.2 company prior to his discharged from the hospital.
Ex.P19 is the bill, it shows that petitioner has purchased the requited equipments of worth Rs.12,000/- for his treatment.
Petitioner has tender medical bills and they are collectively marked as Ex.P.20 and it reveals that petitioner has spent Rs.1,61,454/- for his medical expenses.
Apparently petitioner has not tendered the medical bills to show that he has paid Rs.1,10,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.

Petitioner himself admitted that insurance company has paid full medical bills amount of Rs.90,00,000/- to the concerned hospitals and out the said amount petitioner has repaid Rs.11,57,880/- to the insurance company.
The aforesaid fact is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.2.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
13.

Petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Columbia Asia and Manipal hospital,
Bangalore as per Ex.P.11 to 14 nearly for a period of ten months.
Further as per Ex.P.19 and 20, he has spent Rs.1,73,455/- for his medical expenses and related medical equipments.

Vaibhav Saha vs Koushik C on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186624589/
4 14.

Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment for more than 10 months as inpatient in two hospitals, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses at least Rs.1,500/- per day.

Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.1,73,455/- and Rs.11,57,880/-
(refunded to insurance company as per Ex.P.17 ) = Rs.13,31,335/-, I award Rs.4,50,000/-.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.17,81,335/- compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
15.

It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained severe traumatic brain injury,
multiple fractures, deep vain thrombosis, that is blood colt in veins, and aspiration pneumonia that is lungs infection.

During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period period of ten months, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
Therefore I award Rs.5,00,000/- under these conventional heads.

16. In the cross examination of PW-1 he admitted that he has received the salary while he was under treatment and further counsel appearing for the petitioner admit that the petitioner is still receiving the salary from his company for the reason that petitioner is an old employee in the Wipro company.
Petitioner has not chosen to place the evidence on record to show that he has lost his future income and the increment details.
Such being the case, there is no loss of income to the petitioner during the laid up period.

17. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has relied on the authorities as noted at Sl. No.1 to 3, at para No.6, wherein it is held that, if the claimant is continue in the service / job then question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.
18. Further in the authorities stated at Sl No.4 and 5, wherein it is held that petitioner cannot claim the medical bills amount which is already paid by the insurer under the medi-claim policy.
In the present case the medical bills amount of Rs.90,00,000/- is paid by the insurer is excluded.
Further respondent No.2 has not probabilise the fact that the bills amount as per Ex.P19 and 20 are included in Rs.90,00,000/- and further he has not disputed the aforesaid bills amount.
Accordingly the aforesaid bills are considered.
With great respect to the aforesaid authorities and the principles laid down therein is considered in the present case.
Except the aforesaid heads petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
1
Pecuniary damages Rs.17,81,335/- 3 Non pecuniary damages Rs. 5,00,000/- 4 TOTAL Rs.22,81,335/-
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,81,335/- only.

5 19.
Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
20. Liability:

The respondent no.2 is the insurer of offending vehicle and the validity of the said policy is not in disputed, and respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate his contention as contended in the written statement.

Inasmuch respondent no.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest,
therefore respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 30 days of judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 affirmative and Issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
21. Issue No.3;
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.22,81,335/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw 60% of the compensation amount with interest, and balance 40%, shall be deposited in nationalized bank for a period of three years.
Issue intimation to the banker not to allow the petitioner to create encumbrance on the deposited amount and not to permit him for premature withdrawal of the deposit amount.

Petitioner has to comply the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt.
17.01.2020, while withdrawing his share of compensation amount with interest.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed off.
Draw award accordingly.
